**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part**: Sugarcane leaf, close-up view
- **Key features**:
  - A prominent cream/white bleached stripe running longitudinally along the midrib/central vein area
  - Green tissue retained on both lateral margins
  - A distinct reddish-brown lesion in the lower-center of the leaf
  - The bleached area appears almost scalded or water-soaked in texture

**Reasoning through classes:**

- **Leaf_Scald** (*Xanthomonas albilineans*): Causes characteristic cream-to-white pencil-line or broad stripes running parallel to leaf veins, giving a "scalded" appearance. The midrib and surrounding tissue become bleached/cream-white while margins remain green. Red/brown necrotic lesions can develop alongside. This matches the image very closely.
- **Yellow_Leaf**: Midrib yellowing (golden-yellow), not cream/white bleaching. Less likely.
- **Brown_Spot**: Discrete oval/circular brown spots — the reddish lesion fits partially, but the dominant cream stripe does not.
- **Pokkah_Boeng**: Associated with distorted/twisted young leaves and chlorotic streaks — no distortion visible here.
- Other classes (mosaic, streak, grassy shoot, sett rot, yellow spot) don't match the dominant bleached-stripe pattern.

The broad cream/white longitudinal stripe along the midrib with retained green margins and a necrotic red lesion is the hallmark of **Leaf Scald**.
